A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERC and discourse-marker study despite the changed title. All 18 pages of v2 and 21 pages of v3, including figures, tables and Appendices A–C, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original IEMOCAP recognition experiments, ten-seed ablations, context analyses and discourse-marker corpus statistics, including supplementary results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds MELD experiments, Transformer comparisons and controlled discourse-marker analyses.

M1.justification: The principal FLAT/HIER encoders, pooling, MLP/LSTM classifiers and lexical fusion procedure remain unchanged. The Transformer is introduced as an ablation comparator, not a replacement. Relabeling SenticNet 7 as 8 does not establish a different fusion algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual evaluation on MELD: seven-way recognition in short, multi-party television dialogue, extending the earlier IEMOCAP-only coverage of acted dyadic conversations. DailyDialog remains proposed future work.

E2.justification: New Table 4 evaluates a two-layer Transformer aggregator against the LSTM on MELD and IEMOCAP. The external comparator sets and scores in v2 Tables 3–4 are retained in v3 Tables 5–6.

E3.justification: v3 adds short-context MELD evaluations at K=0,5,10, matched aggregator comparisons and discourse-marker analyses controlling for length, speaker and elicitation condition. MELD reports patience 10 despite claiming an identical protocol; IEMOCAP retains patience 60/20. SenticNet's stated version changes from 7 to 8 without evidence of reruns.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether saturation depends on the LSTM aggregator and whether discourse-marker associations survive confound controls. Section 4.4 also adds Happy–Excited marker-profile similarity evidence. The layer, pooling and SenticNet analyses in Appendices B–C remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 adds progressive covariate-adjusted mixed-effects estimation and a marker-profile correlation analysis. Figure 3 changes uncertainty bands from SD to SE. Table 2 supplies four previously absent SDs, discloses one nine-seed cell and explains remaining missing SDs. Table 4 distinguishes ten-seed comparisons from single-seed diagnostics; these disclosures do not establish increased runs.

E6.justification: New results include MELD FLAT/HIER weighted F1 of 59.22/61.48 at K=0 and 59.07/60.91 at K=10, aggregator comparisons, adjusted discourse-marker coefficients and Happy–Excited correlation r=0.990. Figure 3 also changes the plotted F1 curves and reports saturation values. Headline IEMOCAP scores and appendix results are retained.

T1.justification: The context-window definition, 90%-gain saturation criterion, discourse-periphery thresholds and appendix fusion formula are retained. The added statistical analyses and intuitive LSTM explanations introduce no new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, RQ4 and conclusion narrow the generation-oriented framing to descriptive discourse evidence, explicitly leaving generation untested. v3 adds claims of cross-dataset relevance and confound-robust Sad marker positioning, while locating the clearest utterance-only hierarchical advantage on MELD.

C2.justification: v3 interprets late context maxima as plateau noise, emphasizes corpus-dependent context requirements and narrows the controlled marker interpretation primarily to Sad. It qualifies the SenticNet null result by fusion method and adds substantive clinical-use, linguistic-transfer and emotional-monitoring limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository address, plus Transformer architecture and MELD configuration details. It identifies the lexical resource as SenticNet 8 rather than 7. Existing software, hardware and principal training details remain; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: The cited-work inventory is retained. v3 more explicitly distinguishes its simple-fusion null result from graph- or attention-based knowledge integration associated with Zhong et al. and Tu et al., and positions its linguistic contribution as descriptive rather than generative.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, updates front matter, revises selected abstract, motivation, discussion and conclusion passages, inserts a MELD subsection, fixes unresolved table references and removes acknowledgements. The main section sequence, much existing prose and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redesigned: peak-context bars become saturation-context bars, with a highlighted context window, gain annotations and revised axes, legend and caption. Two new tables present MELD and aggregator results, and Table 2 gains explanatory uncertainty notes. Other figures and appendix tables are retained.

improvement.justification: MELD validation, confound controls, clearer uncertainty reporting and narrower generation claims address weaknesses in v2. However, important new evidence is inconsistently interpreted: Table 3 retains HIER advantages of 2.12 and 1.84 points at K=5 and K=10 despite claims that the advantage vanishes. Figure 3 annotates an Angry gain of 14.2 points while Section 4.3 retains 8.34 without reconciliation. These discrepancies affect central conclusions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
